headline: Goldman Sachs says public opposition has barely changed its forecast for how many US data centers will be built through 2027.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: fresh, from a major bank, with concrete numbers and a clear political angle.
importance_line: Local residents, utilities and voters ahead of the 3 Nov midterms are affected, while Goldman's forecast is one bank's estimate and could prove wrong if opposition hardens.
summary: Reuters reports that Goldman Sachs, in a note on Sunday 4 Oct 2026, raised its end-2026 forecast for US data center capacity by 5 gigawatts to 64 and cut its end-2027 forecast by 5 gigawatts to 90 (a gigawatt is a billion watts, roughly one large power plant), and said opposition has not much changed the outlook through 2027. Goldman expects data center power demand to grow 38% in each of 2026 and 2027, even though a June Reuters/Ipsos poll found only 14% of Americans would support an AI data center in their own community.
notes: Read via AOL's copy of Reuters; original Reuters link not shown.
